turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a time during this past year when you felt extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row?
turns.patient_response:
I don't think so. I don't really get extremely happy, and I'm not really an irritable person, unless I'm just tired from work or something. 

But talking about being irritable... the new hostess at work is always so irritable. She sighs every time someone asks her a question, like it's this huge burden. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she seats a table. It's so distracting when you're trying to take an order and all you hear is *clack clack clack*. I don't know why people wear jewelry that makes noise. Like wind chimes. My neighbor put up these massive wind chimes last week, the kind that look like giant metal pipes. They don't even make a pretty twinkling sound, they just gong like a church bell every time there's a breeze. It's impossible to sleep with the window open now. I love sleeping with the window open, especially in the fall when the air gets really crisp. You can smell the leaves, you know? But raking leaves is the worst. When I was a kid, my dad used to make me rake the whole front yard, and the rake always gave me blisters between my thumb and pointer finger. Band-aids never stay on there either. They always peel off at the edges and get all gross and gray...

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and loose associations, drifting continuously from the topic of irritability to a coworker's bracelets, wind chimes, sleeping with windows open, raking leaves, and band-aids.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies experiencing periods of extreme happiness or being an irritable person.
